subject: physics
title: Waves Adventure 3: Standing waves and resonance
welcome_lead: Today you'll set up standing waves on a string — and resonate.
meta_desc: Physics — standing waves, nodes and antinodes, harmonics, open/closed pipes, resonance.
final_note: You learned standing waves form from two oppositely travelling waves; harmonics: λ_n = 2L/n for fixed string; resonance amplifies at natural frequencies.

concepts.def: Forced f = natural f → large amplitude

walkthroughs.body_html:
String fixed at both ends — nodes at ends.

Fundamental: λ₁ = 2L, f₁ = v/(2L).

nth harmonic: λ_n = 2L/n, f_n = nv/(2L).

Wave speed on string: v = √(T/μ), where T = tension, μ = mass/length.

Both ends open: antinodes at ends.
f_n = nv/(2L), n = 1, 2, 3,.

One closed end: node at closed, antinode at open.
f_n = nv/(4L), n = 1, 3, 5,. (odd harmonics only).

Explains why a closed pipe an octave lower than open of same L.

System has natural frequency f_0. Driving at f_0 → amplitude grows large — resonance.

- Pushing a swing in sync.
- Tacoma Narrows Bridge collapse 1940 (resonance from wind).
- MRI machines: nuclear magnetic resonance.

Damping reduces resonance peak.
